reading.text:
Reading for PaperWeakTuple (paper: an element of Hweak, §3 "Solution space").
Hweak := L^2(0,T;R^n) x L^2(0,T;R^m) x H^2_W(0,T;R^{m x d}) x H^2_N(0,T;L^2(nu;R^m)), where
L^2(0,T;R^j) := {V cadlag adapted, E int_0^T |V_t|^2 dt < inf},
H^2_W := {Z predictable R^{m x d}: E int_0^T |Z_t|_F^2 dt < inf},
H^2_N := {U predictable L^2(nu;R^m)-valued: E int_0^T ||U_t||^2 dt < inf} (via a P (x) calE-measurable
representative). Adaptedness/predictability are w.r.t. the standing filtration (usual
augmentation of sigma(W,N,F_0)). Elements are equivalence classes (indistinguishable / a.e.).
Faithful Lean: a predicate on (X, Y, Z, U) recording cadlag paths (every path or a.s.; with usual
conditions, a.s.-cadlag and adapted is equivalent up to indistinguishability), adaptedness, the
dt dP square integrability (integrals over [0,T], not over all of R), predictability of Z (w.r.t.
the predictable sigma-field on Omega x [0,T]) and of U jointly with the mark (P (x) calE), and the
finite energies. It may additionally carry X_T in L^2 if the solution notion needs it (paper's
terminal law). It must not require E sup < inf.

comparison.text:
Comparison for PaperWeakTuple (System/PaperWeakSolution.lean:80).
Fields: X_adapted (X_{i,t} F_t-measurable for t in [0,T]); X_rightCont (every path right-continuous at
every t in [0,T)); X_leftLim (a.s. every path has left limits at every t in (0,T]); X_sq (energy
E int_0^T X_{i,t}^2 dt finite, the energy being the lintegral over [0,T] of |.|^2 w.r.t. P x Leb);
the same for Y; Z_pred (each coordinate predictable for the predictable sigma-algebra generated by
(-inf,0] x A, A in F_0, and (r,inf) x A, A in F_r), Z_vanish off [0,T], Z_sq (finite energy); U_pred (each
coordinate marked predictable: sigma-algebra generated by F x (r,q] x B, F in F_r, r >= 0, nu(B) < inf),
U_vanish off [0,T], U_sq (finite marked energy E int_0^T int_E U^2 nu ds).
Against my reading of Hweak = L^2(0,T;R^n) x L^2(0,T;R^m) x H^2_W x H^2_N: cadlag adapted X, Y with
dt dP square integrability on [0,T] -- yes (coordinatewise finite energy = finite E int |X|^2 since
finitely many coordinates); Z predictable square integrable -- yes; U predictable (P (x) calE) square
integrable -- yes (the marked predictable sigma-algebra equals P (x) calE on times > 0 for sigma-finite
nu; the time-0 slice is a Lebesgue-null time). No E sup requirement -- correct. No X_T in L^2 -- the
paper's Hweak does not contain it; it is carried by the solution predicates. Adaptedness is for the
given filtration F (the propositions instantiate the paper's augmented filtration).
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices (harmless):
1. Processes are families of real coordinate processes indexed by all of R; only [0,T] is
   constrained for X, Y; Z and U are normalised to vanish off [0,T].
2. Cadlag is encoded as: every path right-continuous on [0,T), left limits a.s. on (0,T]; this class is
   closed under indistinguishability, which is how the paper identifies elements; every paper element
   has such a representative.
3. The marked predictable sigma-algebra has no time-0 cells (so U_0 = 0 is forced, as is Z_0 = 0 by the
   vanishing before 0); time 0 is Lebesgue-null, so every paper (Z, U) has an a.e.-equal version in
   the class and no integral changes.
4. Square integrability is coordinatewise finite energy, equivalent to the paper's norms for
   finitely many coordinates.
